quizzes.stem: A team wants a review command that every developer has after cloning the repository. Where does the file go?

options.a: In a settings file that holds a list of commands for Claude Code
options.b: In a commands folder in each developer's home directory, created by hand
options.c: In the root instructions file, under a heading that names the review checklist
options.d: In the project's own configuration folder, committed with the sources

explanation.d: A command file in the project's own folder is committed and reaches every clone.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a home folder is personal: "commands in the home folder are personal".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the memory file holds instructions and not definitions: "the memory file is for instructions and context".
explanation.a: Ruled out because no such mechanism exists: "A `commands` array in a config file is a mechanism that does not exist".

quizzes.stem: React components use hooks, handlers use async/await, models follow a repository pattern, and test files sit beside the code they test in every folder. Which setup applies the right conventions automatically, test files included?

options.a: A rule per concern, each scoped by a glob that matches names
options.b: One root file with a section for each area, left for Claude to apply as it sees fit
options.c: A skill for each area, which developers start with a slash command
options.d: A memory file in each folder that holds the conventions of that folder

explanation.a: Rules with globs reach files by their names, wherever they sit.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the model would have to infer the section: "One root file with a section per area leaves Claude to infer which section applies."
explanation.c: Ruled out because a path match starts nothing in a skill: "a skill is invoked, or chosen by the model from its description, and a path match does not start it".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a file is bound to its directory: "each file is bound to its directory, and test files next to their sources are in all of them".

quizzes.stem: A 400-line root memory file is split into five files that the root file imports. What happens to the context cost?

options.a: It falls to a fifth, since each piece loads when needed
options.b: It doubles, as every piece is read once by the root and once again
options.c: It does not change, since everything referenced is read at the start
options.d: It falls in any session that never touches the files the pieces describe

explanation.c: Imports organise a file and do not cut its cost.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the load is at launch: "imported files also load at launch".
explanation.b: Ruled out because nothing is read twice; the page says only that they "don't reduce its context cost".
explanation.d: Ruled out because an import is not conditional on touched files; only a rule with a `paths` list is: "A rule with a `paths` list loads when Claude works with a file that matches one of its globs".

quizzes.stem: A developer must turn a monolith into services: dozens of files change and the service boundaries are undecided. Which approach fits?

options.a: Begin with direct edits, and let the boundaries show as work proceeds
options.b: Explore in plan mode first, and settle the design before any edit
options.c: Write complete instructions for each service, then execute them directly
options.d: Execute directly, and switch to plan mode only if the work turns complicated

explanation.b: Many files, open boundaries and design decisions point to planning first.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the boundaries are what to find first: "risks rework when a dependency turns up late".
explanation.c: Ruled out because instructions would assume the structure: "the instructions would assume the structure, and the structure is what has to be found by exploring".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the stem already holds the complexity: "ignores that the complexity is in the stem already".

quizzes.stem: A developer asks for a function that validates e-mail addresses and has no way yet to tell whether the first version is right. What should be added to the request?

options.a: A longer description of what a valid address looks like, in prose
options.b: A request to explain the function after writing it, line by line
options.c: A reminder to be careful and to check the work before it finishes
options.d: A few input and expected-result pairs, with an instruction to run them

explanation.d: A pair of input and expected result is a check that Claude can run.
explanation.a: Ruled out because prose leaves cases open: "Two or three cases with their expected results say what a paragraph of description leaves open."
explanation.c: Ruled out because a reminder is not a signal: "'looks done' is the only signal available".
explanation.b: Ruled out because an explanation checks nothing: "Give Claude a check it can run: tests, a build, a screenshot to compare."

quizzes.stem: A developer has corrected the same mistake three times in one long session, and the fourth attempt is wrong again. What is the next step?

options.a: Add a fourth correction with the same wording but in capital letters
options.b: Clear the conversation, then restart with a prompt that holds what was learned
options.c: Keep the session, since the earlier history helps Claude see the pattern
options.d: Switch to plan mode for the rest of the session so that nothing is edited at all

explanation.b: After two failed corrections the context holds failed approaches, so a clean start with a better prompt works better.
explanation.a: Ruled out because emphasis does not clear the context: "the context is now full of failed approaches".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the history is the problem: "the history is now failed approaches, and a clean session with a better prompt does better".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the mode does not remove the clutter: "A clean session with a better prompt almost always outperforms a long session with accumulated corrections."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2, a team using Claude Code on a shared codebase. A rule file for the handlers lists `paths: src/api` and never seems to apply when handlers are edited. What is the cause?

options.a: Rule files are read only when a session is first started
options.b: A bare folder name is no glob, so nothing is matched
options.c: Handlers are covered by the command folder, which takes priority
options.d: The path needs the word handlers in it for the rule to be found

explanation.b: A bare folder name is not a glob.
explanation.a: Ruled out because path-scoped rules load when a matching file is read: "A rule with a `paths` list loads when Claude works with a file that matches one of its globs".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the command folder holds commands and not conventions: "A command file in the project, `.claude/commands/review.md`, committed to the repository".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the match is by glob on file paths and not by a word: "`**` crosses folders and `*` stays inside one".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2, a team using Claude Code on a shared codebase. A developer's habit of replying in short sentences is added to the shared root memory file, and colleagues object. Where should it go?

options.a: In a personal instructions document kept out of version control
options.b: In the review command, which each person runs in their own way
options.c: In a rule scoped by glob to the developer's own commits
options.d: In the settings as a permission rule that the others can override

explanation.a: A preference of one person belongs in a personal file.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a glob cannot select one developer's commits: "A preference of one developer".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the command is shared by all: "A command file in the project, `.claude/commands/review.md`, committed to the repository".
explanation.d: Ruled out because permission rules are for what Claude may do and not for style: "A permission rule or a hook".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2, a team using Claude Code on a shared codebase. The team wants to be sure that no session ever reads the environment file, whatever the model decides. Which control gives that?

options.a: A deny rule in the permission settings, or a hook that blocks the call
options.b: A scoped instruction that repeats the prohibition for that file
options.c: An entry in the modes table that sends such requests to plan mode
options.d: A line in the root memory that forbids reading the environment file

explanation.a: Code that runs holds whatever the model decides.
explanation.d: Ruled out because a sentence is a request: "treats them as context, not enforced configuration".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a rule is the same kind of text: "To block an action regardless of what Claude decides, use a PreToolUse hook instead."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the table advises on mode and enforces nothing: "Plan mode tells Claude to research and propose changes without making them."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2, a team using Claude Code on a shared codebase. A large feature has unclear requirements, and the developer is unsure what to ask for. Which start fits?

options.a: Ask for the most likely reading to be built, then fix it after a careful review
options.b: Ask for three complete versions, and choose the one that looks best
options.c: Have the assistant interview the user, write a spec, run it in a clean session
options.d: Ask for the tests to be written last, so that they match what was built

explanation.c: The missing piece is a decision only the people can make, so the questions come first.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a guess builds on the wrong reading: "the missing piece is not a design that Claude could find in the code, it is a decision only the people can make".
explanation.b: Ruled out because three versions do not settle what is wanted: "Claude stops when the work looks done".
explanation.d: Ruled out because tests that follow the code are no target: "A failing test that describes the behaviour is a target."
